hed: DOJ issues new Florida grand jury subpoenas in probe of Trump-Russia investigators
dek: The Associated Press reported that the Justice Department is demanding testimony before a Florida grand jury in an investigation pursuing a theory that intelligence-community officials who scrutinized Donald Trump — including over Russian interference in the 2016 election — conspired against him and violated his rights. New subpoenas to former government officials mark an escalation in a year-long inquiry; Joe diGenova is counseling the attorney general on the effort. It was not immediately clear how many witnesses had been served or whether charges will follow.

byline: Event summary from public reporting and named outlets

cl.body: AP, the Los Angeles Times, and News4Jax/AP emphasize new Florida grand-jury subpoenas, a loosely defined IC-conspiracy theory, and uncertainty over witness identities and charges.

cr.body: Fox News Russiagate coverage, the Washington Examiner’s Florida DOJ reporting, and News4Jax wire accounts frame accountability for alleged Russia-probe abuses as the Florida grand jury escalates with fresh subpoenas.

seo_description: AP reports the Justice Department is demanding Florida grand jury testimony in a probe alleging an intelligence-community conspiracy against Trump tied to the 2016 Russia inquiry.
